title: AI Bottlenecks and Value Capture
proposition: When cognition gets cheaper, growth can be limited by demand, delivery, or authorization. Easing a constraint creates value; competition and contracts determine who keeps it.
network_intro: The bottleneck is whichever constraint prevents a workflow from producing more accepted results. It can differ across businesses and change over time.

stages.title: Cheaper cognitive tasks
stages.body: More tasks become affordable and more firms can enter.

stages.title: Other constraints bind
stages.body: Demand, delivery capacity, or authorization limits sales.

stages.title: Bargaining power shifts
stages.body: Control of the scarce input may give its owner better terms.

stages.title: Supply responds
stages.body: Investment and substitutes can ease the constraint and move it elsewhere.

feedbacks.title: Concentration
feedbacks.body: Profits can fund acquisitions, capacity expansion, and customer lock-in, strengthening the incumbent’s position.

feedbacks.title: Diffusion
feedbacks.body: High returns attract competitors and substitutes. Common standards can make switching easier.

feedback_note: Supply growth can reduce concentration. Customer lock-in and hard-to-replace assets can sustain it.
model_intro: Choose a task with fixed quality, deadline, and responsibility requirements. Measure demand and both capacities in accepted tasks per month.
assumptions: All inputs are illustrative. Price and fixed costs are held constant. Changing the contribution margin changes variable cost. Expansion and governance costs are not included.
model_limit: The model assumes each input is necessary and cannot be substituted. Actual sales may be lower than capacity. It does not describe the whole economy.
margin_warning: At a negative contribution margin, each additional task increases the loss. Reducing or stopping delivery may be preferable.

capture_rows.creates: Reach customers with a useful result they will pay for
capture_rows.captures: Customer relationships, renewals, channel terms, switching costs
capture_rows.erodes: Platform bundling, price competition, easier switching

capture_rows.creates: Provide the resources needed for reliable delivery
capture_rows.captures: Scarce capacity, data rights, financing and supply contracts
capture_rows.erodes: New capacity, substitutes, capital costs, outdated data

capture_rows.creates: Put results into use with enforceable permissions and clear responsibility
capture_rows.captures: Integration across organizations and customers willing to pay for it
capture_rows.erodes: Built-in platform features, open standards, insufficient paid demand

tests.title: Agent trust
tests.hypothesis: Authorization or acceptance may limit a cross-organization workflow.
tests.test: Shorten approvals without changing task quality or customer budgets. Track paid, accepted tasks, review time, and net savings.
tests.weakens: If sales do not rise, or customers choose bundled platform tools over a paid service, authorization may not be the binding constraint or a viable standalone business.

tests.title: Startup viability
tests.hypothesis: New firms may enter faster than sustainable businesses emerge.
tests.test: Follow firms founded in the same period and market. Track repeat customers, operating viability, shareholder returns, and spillovers separately.
tests.weakens: Success rates need a defined cohort, observation period, and outcome. The model does not assume a fixed number of winners.

tests.title: Value distribution
tests.hypothesis: Cheaper delivery does not guarantee higher application profits.
tests.test: Track delivery costs, prices, upstream fees, human review, retention, and margins within the same firms.
tests.weakens: Broad, sustained profit growth unrelated to control of customers or scarce inputs would weaken this explanation of value distribution.

case_intro: Pension and sovereign investments show how ownership affects the distribution of AI returns. The case compares investment routes and household exposure.
